title: Should AI reverse engineered game be allowed on this sub?
author: Timely_Craft1721
selftext:
Honestly, AI reverse engineered game are the worst lot to come out of this sub. They dont come up with their own concept and just copy another games concept and then paste it as their own. the AI-made clones showing up on this sub are one of the reasons I’ve been hesitant to share my own game.

I don’t have a problem with developers taking inspiration from other games. That’s always been part of game development. But copying someone’s work with AI blatantly, and just making a few surface-level changes, and presenting it as your own feels pretty shameless.

It’s discouraging to spend months developing an idea, knowing someone could see a post about it and churn out a cheap imitation in a day. The copy might lack the depth or care of the original, but it still makes sharing your progress feel like a risk.

I hope Steam and other platforms find better ways to deal with blatant clones. I’d love to share what I’m working on, but seeing this stuff makes me reluctant to post it here.

comments.author: Solarka45

Cloning is bad.

comments.author: llothar
comments.body: What about upgraded versions of old games? Think Open Transport Tycoon Deluxe or ZDoom. I literally asked Opus 5.5 to redo me my childhood favourite, the 1995 Space Federation/Star Reach game in Godot. Within 24h it made a pixel perfect clone. It still needs original assets, but now it is higher resolution, has full mouse support, and it can even be played on Android if I fancy it.

comments.author: gajop
comments.body:
Copying concept and reverse engineering are two distinct things.
Copying concepts and even IP from games as "demos" of what AI can do is imo fine. We know you can't sell your Mario/Zelda/WoW clone but showing what's doable and in what time is a useful reference. Better yet if you include the tools and approaches (and hopefully it isn't just one big fat prompt)

Copying games by actual reverse engineering...idk, I don't think it's so common, outside of emulators or what not, and that's fine, keeps dead games playable.

For small indies I would be a bit reluctant to say yes, but if it's a small indie no one really heard of your game anyway, and big ones need no protection.

Unfortunately I think people will steal your game idea, whether it happens on this sub or not isn't important. If I were you, I'd be reluctant with sharing game ideas that can be easily copied.

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body: You actually can own an idea: Nemesis system.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
Patents aren't owning an idea, it is an legal protection that exist to help businesses pursue an idea for an limited time, without contest.

Ir is very specific, as in do you even know what the Nemesis system is legally? You could make an game with orcs fighting for rankings, and positions in their culture, even using the cut-scenes, and that would not be the Nemesis system. Game developers could already have made games with Nemesis clones, if they took the time to learn what the Nemesis system is.

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body:
There is multiple games who uses parts of it sure, but none of them uses the whole idea, would you bet a multimillion project on that you can copy the whole nemesis system? 

Plus I do not agree with the clones are fine. There is a difference between using an idea and copy an exact game. Most of post I see here are not just clones of idea, they literally try to clone exact games. Now this is fun and anything, expect when you worked on your game for long time you designed it etc. you release it and in five days 10 other clones of your game spawn.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
>but none of them uses the whole idea,

Because that would be the same game right, I mean even when the nemesis system is finally released from it's patent, I don't think there is any game ideas that would use it. As using it would just turn your game into Shadow of Mordor.

The Nemesis system is specific to the point where exact events are required. It makes far more sense to borrow pieces of the idea.

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
Enough people make clones of a game and it's become a new video game genre. 

How many games are based top down 3D isometrics based on Diablo?   
How many games are 1st person shooters based on Doom?  
How many games are based on RPG worlds which started with Fallout 1 and 2.   
Dungeon Crawlers started with Wizardry.   
Minecraft was actually something unique which didn't exist before.   
Card battlers came from card collections games like Pokémon and Magic: the gathering.   
Turned based party RPGs from Baldor's Gate 1 & 2. 

You get the idea, all major game genres came from something original that copied or cloned from the base idea. 

Eventually, there will be so many slop clones they will get ignored and people will be forced to come up with something original and polished to make any money at all.

The Video game market, smartphone app, short form content and netflix libraries are already oversaturated. 

After a slopocalypse good game will arise from the ashes. Just let people go through the process. There will be great games made with AI tool in the near future.

comments.author: davidslv
comments.body:
This is not something new in the industry. The examples I can think of right now are Flappy Bird, was a simple concept, was addictive, repetitive and once it was sunsetted by the developer, I don’t even know how many copies came out on App Store with their flavour, it was also used as teaching material in some learning platforms. Another is 1024 and 2048, how many variants have we seen since it came out?

Those predate AI, yet, it didn’t stop anyone from learning, creating and sharing - some even monetising. 

I recently looked at App Store and Nintendo eShop, most games seemed put together so fast that they just don’t appeal to me, then slapped with ads to keep them free or load them with in-app purchases… 

I don’t want any of that in my games, maybe an expansion pack of value but not let me buy more carrots as currency to buy other in game items and such… 

Most of us are not professionals in the industry, we have a dream, painful one, to one day make a game, everyone has to start somewhere and that somewhere today, with the least amount of friction to many is using AI. 

I don’t think many people are interested in the distribution, that isn’t why many of us come here (or elsewhere) to share, it’s more a feeling of accomplishment and move on to the next thing and take something with them perhaps some learning during the journey to the final result.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
It's complex and nuanced.  
  
True reverse engineering from the game files: yes, I'd be for a ban.  
  
Porting the game to a new platform or making it work again in modern times: that's fine as long as you provide that as something where somebody still needs the original game files separately.  
  
Using an existing game as the target state for development: I think that's fine for only demo and the lolz, as long as they don't actually publish it.

comments.author: SplinterOfChaos
comments.body:
>It’s discouraging to spend months developing an idea, knowing someone could see a post about it and churn out a cheap imitation in a day.

I used to spend *years* on projects and now I'm watching people finish projects in weeks, then complain about how their effort aren't being respected. :/

The fact that AI makes it so easy to implement things just by describing it is causing a real distortion of ownership. Making clones has been an industry norm since the 90's, but programmers wouldn't know how to implement things properly, artists might have different styles, and designers would make changes without understanding why/how the original system worked. These days, we don't malign games for being "clones" so much because all games are more similar to each other than they used to be.

But now with AI, making clones is much more viable and many of the human elements which guaranteed uniqueness are being replaced by automation which trends towards sameness.
